title: Library
lead: Ready material from open sources for every field, from business, law and medicine to engineering and the arts, mostly in English: decks, word lists, question sets, courses and videos, textbooks and books. Each one says its licence and where it comes from.

filter.subject: Field
filter.more: More filters: level, certificate, video, licence

licence.cc-by-sa: Free, with credit and the same licence (CC BY-SA)
licence.free-pictures: Free: text in the public domain, pictures under free licences
licence.free-access: Free to read or watch at its source
licence.gfdl: Free, with credit and the same licence (GNU FDL)
licence.cc-by-nd: Free to share unchanged, with credit (CC BY-ND)

why.nonCommercial: Free for non-commercial use, so AnyLearn does not copy it: open it at the source.
why.noLicence: It gives no licence, so AnyLearn does not copy it: open it at the source, then bring its file to Decks.
why.bringFile: Open the papers at the source, then upload one in Quiz → Exams → Upload a past paper.
why.textbook: Read it at its source, or download its PDF and upload the chapters you need to a knowledge base (a file of up to 50 MB and 400 pages).
why.textbookNonCommercial: Read it at its source, or download its PDF. Its licence allows only non-commercial use: upload the chapters you need to a knowledge base for your own study (a file of up to 50 MB and 400 pages).
why.enrol: Free to take at its source, where you enrol; AnyLearn does not copy it.
why.chooseLesson: Free to reuse, one lesson at a time: open it, choose a lesson, then add its address to a knowledge base with Add a link.

items.upWords: English terms a programmer meets, by language (Python, Go, JavaScript and more): words only, to look up and save.
items.upGuide: A book on learning methods: state, cycles, evidence and review, with worksheets.
items.khan: Short video lessons and practice in maths, science and more, in many languages.
items.thptName: Vietnamese high school graduation exam papers
items.thpt: The Ministry of Education's reference and past papers, by subject.
items.body: Exercises by muscle and equipment, each with its steps, to use in your plan.
items.voa: News and stories in slower, simpler English, with audio, video and transcripts, at three levels.
items.wikibooksEsl: An open book of English lessons for learners: grammar, vocabulary and everyday phrases.
items.storybooks: Short illustrated stories at five levels, read aloud, with the same story in many other languages.
items.usaLearns: A free English course with video lessons for everyday life and work, from beginner up.

empty: Nothing matches. Try any kind, any subject or all languages.
deckFull: Not added: you have the most cards allowed. Delete a deck first.
linkAdded: Added to {{name}}. It is read in the background.
feedAdded: Followed as a feed in {{name}}: its videos are added as they come.
credit: Each item names its source and licence. AnyLearn ships only what a licence allows it to; the rest opens at its source.

credits.fpb: The courses and books are listed by free-programming-books (Free Ebook Foundation, CC BY 4.0); each belongs to its author.
credits.gutenberg: The books are from Project Gutenberg and are in the public domain in the United States; check your country's law before using them elsewhere.
credits.otl: The textbooks are listed by the Open Textbook Library (Center for Open Education, University of Minnesota); each has its own licence, shown with it, and belongs to its authors.
credits.mit: The courses are MIT OpenCourseWare's, under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, listed from MIT Learn; they open at MIT.

awesome.math: Listed by awesome-math (rossant/awesome-math, CC0); each link belongs to its owner.
awesome.certificates: Listed by awesome-certificates (PanXProject/awesome-certificates, CC0); each course belongs to its provider, and its certificate is the provider's to give.
awesome.youtubers: Listed by awesome-youtubers (JoseDeFreitas/awesome-youtubers, CC0); each channel belongs to its owner, and is added as a feed to choose videos from.

credits.mitx: The courses are MITx Online's, listed from MIT Learn: free to take, with a certificate for a fee; each opens at MIT.

wordsPace: The words come up 20 new a day from today, after any you are already being given.
wordsNone: No new words: you have them all.

wordLists.ngsl: The 2,800 words that make up about 92% of everyday English, most frequent first, each with a definition in easy English.
wordLists.nawl: About 960 words frequent in academic writing that the NGSL leaves out, with definitions in easy English.
wordLists.hsk3: The Chinese proficiency test's words for levels 1 to 9 (HSK 3.0, 2021), with pinyin and English meanings.
wordLists.hsk2: The older HSK's words for levels 1 to 6 (HSK 2.0), with pinyin and English meanings.
wordLists.jlpt: The Japanese-Language Proficiency Test's words as commonly listed for N5 to N1, with readings and English meanings.

addToQuiz: Add to a knowledge base's Quiz
setNone: Nothing new: that knowledge base has this part already.

sets.trivia: Multiple-choice and true-or-false questions on general knowledge, science, history, geography, the arts and more, by category, easiest first.
sets.arc: Grade-school science questions from real tests, multiple choice: Easy, and Challenge, which simple lookups get wrong.
sets.gsm8k: Maths word problems of two to eight steps, answered with a number and marked by value, each with its worked steps.
sets.python: Exercism's Python exercises, easiest first: write the code in the browser and run the tests.

wordsDays: New ones come up from {{first}} to {{last}}.

certificate.free: Free certificate of completion (as the list says)
certificate.badge: Free digital badge (as the list says)
